'''Thisbe Kerstin Lindhorst''' {{postnom|country=GBR|HonFRSC|size=100%}} (born 19 November 1962) is a German biochemist who has been professor of organic chemistry and biochemistry at [[Kiel University]] since 2000.<ref name=Hamburg>{{cite web |title=Kurzbiographie und Publikationen von Thisbe K. Lindhorst |url=https://www.chemie.uni-hamburg.de/institute/oc/publikationen/db/lindhorst.html |website=[[University of Hamburg]] |access-date=4 January 2024 |language=de}}</ref> She was a board member of the [[German Chemical Society]] from 2012 to 2019,<ref name=CV /> and was elected as its president from 2016 to 2017. Her research focuses on [[glycoscience]]s and the function of the [[glycocalyx]].<ref name=Giessen>{{cite web |title=Guest lecture by Prof. Dr. rer. nat. Thisbe Lindhorst: Modern Perspectives in the Glycosciences |url=https://www.uni-giessen.de/de/fbz/zentren/ggl/curriculum/ccf/perspec/cvlindhorst |website=[[Giessen University]] |access-date=4 January 2024 |date=3 December 2015}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Lindhorst was born on 19 November 1962 in [[Munich]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Lindhorst, Thisbe |url=https://www.hpk.uni-hamburg.de/resolve/id/cph_person_00003788 |website=[[University of Hamburg]] |access-date=4 January 2024}}</ref> She studied chemistry at [[LMU Munich]] from 1981 to 1984 and chemistry with biochemistry at the [[University of Münster]] from 1985 to 1987.<ref name=CV>{{cite web |title=Research Profile/CV Prof. Dr. Thisbe K. Lindhorst |url=http://scholle.oc.uni-kiel.de/lind/TKL_CV_Jan2019.pdf |website=[[Kiel University]] |access-date=4 January 2024 |date=January 2019}}</ref> She achieved a [[PhD]] at the [[University of Hamburg]] in 1991,<ref name=Giessen /> with a thesis on the inhibitors of [[fucose]] [[metabolism]].<ref name=AN>{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Thisbe K. Lindhorst |url=https://www.academia-net.org/profile/thisbe-k-lindhorst/80017 |website=[[AcademiaNet]] |access-date=4 January 2024}}</ref>

She undertook her [[postdoctorate]] at the [[University of British Columbia]] in [[Vancouver]], [[Canada]] from 1992, focusing on carbohydrates and [[dendrimer]]s,<ref name=AN /> before returning to Hamburg to earn her [[habilitation]] in 1998.<ref name=Giessen />

==Career==
In 2000, Lindhorst was appointed Full Professor of Organic Chemistry at [[Kiel University]]; she was the first woman to hold the post since the [[Second World War]].<ref name=IUPAC>{{cite web |title=International Award for Thisbe K. Lindhorst |url=https://www.uni-kiel.de/en/university/details/news/international-award-for-thisbe-k-lindhorst |website=[[Kiel University]] |access-date=4 January 2024 |date=14 March 2017}}</ref>

In 2015, Lindhorst was elected president of the [[German Chemical Society]] (GDCh) for the 2016–2017 term.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Renate Hoer |title=Thisbe K. Lindhorst wird neue GDCh-Präsidentin |url=https://www.gdch.de/service-information/nachricht/article/thisbe-k-lindhorst-wird-neue-gdch-praesidentin.html |website=[[German Chemical Society]] |access-date=4 January 2024 |language=de |date=23 September 2015}}</ref> She was second women to hold the position in the society's 150-year history.<ref name=IUPAC2 />

As part of the society's anniversary commemorations in 2017, Lindhorst co-edited ''Unendliche Weiten: Kreuz und quer durchs Chemie-Universum'', a book covering the implications of modern chemistry to everyday life, with [[Hans-Jürgen Quadbeck-Seeger]].<ref name=IUPAC2 /><ref>{{cite web |title=Unendliche Weiten: Kreuz und quer durchs Chemie-Universum |url=https://www.wiley.com/en-cn/Unendliche+Weiten:+Kreuz+und+quer+durchs+Chemie+Universum-p-9783527342037 |website=[[Wiley (publisher)|Wiley]] |access-date=4 January 2024 |date=March 2017}}</ref> In August 2017, she wrote the editorial for ''[[Angewandte Chemie]]'' celebrating the GDCh's anniversary, noting chemistry's moral and ethical duties, and pushing for "a culture that has the well-being of the entire population and the planet in mind".<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Thisbe K. Lindhorst |title=Chemistry Has a Commitment to Life |journal=[[Angewandte Chemie]] |date=10 August 2017 |volume=56 |issue=37 |pages=10962–10963 |doi=10.1002/anie.201707088 |pmid=28796403 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/anie.201707088 |access-date=4 January 2024}}</ref>

===Research===
Lindhorst is an expert in [[carbohydrate chemistry]] and has written over 150 research papers.<ref name=IUPAC2 /> She has pioneered studies of [[multivalency]] in the [[glycoscience]]s and the importance of the orientation of molecules on cell surfaces for biological recognition.<ref name=IUPAC2 /> Her findings around molecule orientation have potential for [[Cell adhesion|anti-adhesion]] therapies and in [[antimicrobial]] [[drug development]].<ref name=IUPAC2 />

===Honours and awards===
In 1998, Lindhorst was awarded the chemistry prize of the [[Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities]] and the Karl Ziegler funding award.<ref name=Hamburg /> She also won the {{ill|Carl Duisberg Memorial Prize|de|Carl-Duisberg-Gedächtnispreis}} in 2000.<ref name=Hamburg /><ref name=Giessen />

In 2017, Lindhorst was one of 12 women given the [[IUPAC]] Distinguished Women in Chemistry or Chemical Engineering award.<ref name=IUPAC /><ref name=IUPAC2>{{cite web |title=IUPAC Distinguished Women in Chemistry and Chemical Engineering Awards |url=https://iupac.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/WO2017_brochure_20170629.pdf |website=[[IUPAC]] |access-date=4 January 2024 |page=4}}</ref> She was also made an [[Honorary Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry]] in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |title=Our Honorary Fellows |url=https://www.rsc.org/about-us/our-history/our-honorary-fellows/ |website=[[Royal Society of Chemistry]] |access-date=4 January 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Lindhorst has two children, born in 1991 and 1995.<ref name=IUPAC2 />
